claim: Main mud-crack propagation followed effective solid-layer compaction in the directly observed 300 and 800 um pin samples.
evidence_nature: direct in-situ X-ray CT plus published interpretation
material_system: NMC622/CB/PVDF/NMP; 45 wt% solids; binder/CB-rich model formulation
geometry_and_scale: 4 mm steel pin; 300/500/800 um blade gaps
source_location: journal PDF pp.6–9; thesis PDF pp.128–135 / printed 96–103
support_status: supported for 300 and 800 um; 500 um early interval missing
competing_explanation: Different event order under forced-convection LFP drying; compaction plateau is an operational proxy rather than a measured mechanical lock
transfer_limit: 500 um data before about 35–36 min were lost; event order and all times require direct LFP validation.
notes: Central evidence for separating shrink-stop from crack onset without claiming a universal sequence.

defect_or_process: D3 bubble venting to D1 crack
claim: A pre-existing bubble grew then vented and permanently deformed the semi-dry layer; after compaction the same region became the preferred main-crack propagation site.
evidence_nature: direct in-situ X-ray CT with revised journal interpretation
geometry_and_scale: 4 mm pin specimen; one key 800 um sample plus small bubble series
source_location: journal PDF pp.6–9; thesis PDF pp.128 and 131–140 / printed 96 and 99–108
competing_explanation: New bubbles from dissolved gas solvent vapor or cavitation; local CBD defect below image resolution
transfer_limit: Commercial slurry degassing geometry and formulation differ; small sample series gives no population effect size.
notes: Do not label the approximately 55 min venting event as ordinary mud-crack propagation or new-bubble nucleation.

claim: A vertical channel crack reaching the steel substrate was followed by delamination initiating at the crack/substrate intersection.
source_location: journal PDF pp.8–10; thesis PDF pp.134–136 / printed 102–104
competing_explanation: Independent interfacial weakness or binder depletion
transfer_limit: Rigid rough steel pins may amplify delamination relative to flexible aluminium foil; interface toughness must be remeasured.
notes: Separate vertical-crack volume from interface-delamination volume before calculating 3D CIF.

claim: Electrode shrinkage was closer to broadly distributed compaction than to a sharp top-down particle-consolidation front in the studied graphite/PVDF/NMP anode.
geometry_and_scale: about 114 um wet and 61 um dry; 60 mm coating
competing_explanation: A low-permeability surface layer can form without a sharp particle front
transfer_limit: Different particles binder solvent and flux can create stronger stratification in LFP.
notes: Prevents equating final surface enrichment with a macroscopic hard-shell front.

claim: Macroscopic shrinkage can stop while capillary supply continues; late isolated-liquid retention in very thick films was inferred from drying curves rather than directly imaged in this study.
evidence_nature: gravimetric drying curves + author mechanism interpretation
support_status: supported for stage separation; clusters are interpreted
competing_explanation: Diffusion-limited solvent removal without literal isolated clusters
transfer_limit: Chemistry differs but event separation is transferable; the proposed cluster morphology needs direct target imaging.
notes: Requires E2 shrink-stop and E4 liquid-disconnection to be separate model events.

claim: Thickness and evaporation rate affected crack onset severity and adhesion; above a rate range severity rose even when critical thickness no longer fell strongly.
source_location: local PDF pp.7–8 Figs.8–10; detection cutoff limitation p.10
competing_explanation: Binder migration adhesion loss and defect statistics co-vary
transfer_limit: Cannot transfer numerical fluxes or critical thickness to LFP/PVDF/NMP; areas below 0.3 mm2 were excluded.
notes: Motivates separate onset and severity boundaries and reporting detection limits.

claim: High drying rate can cause binder enrichment near the surface and depletion near the current collector with adhesion loss.
competing_explanation: Sedimentation adsorption and measurement method can alter apparent gradient
transfer_limit: Binder and solvent match the target class but active material electrode polarity microstructure and drying geometry differ; use actual evaporation flux rather than oven temperature.
notes: Strong evidence for history dependence but not universality.

claim: Increasing drying temperature was associated with PVDF and conductive-agent movement toward the surface and lower adhesion/higher resistance in the studied cathode.
competing_explanation: Actual flux film thickness particle porosity and adsorption may be controlling variables
transfer_limit: Cathode chemistry and process are not the target commercial LFP line.
notes: Must be read together with E009 counterevidence.

claim: Across room temperature to 120 C the measured F-rich PVDF depth distribution was largely insensitive to drying temperature while fine-carbon redistribution was more evident.
competing_explanation: Measurement sensitivity flux and formulation may mask or change PVDF migration
transfer_limit: Shows that oven temperature alone is not a universal migration coordinate.
notes: Retained as an explicit conflict rather than averaged away.

claim: A published non-steady LFP/PVDF/NMP model generates temperature and drying trends but its internal phase and boundary equations require re-derivation and it does not predict migration voids or fracture.
evidence_nature: model + limited surface-temperature validation + equation audit
target_match: high for chemistry; low for internal state and failure
source_location: local PDF pp.4–6 equations and pp.11–14 validation
support_status: supported only for thermal trend structure
competing_explanation: Unmodelled binder mechanics migration pore evolution and fracture control defects
transfer_limit: Eq.23 gas-phase weighting and Eqs.26–27 heat-flux boundary are apparently inconsistent; k_g/mu_g prose is swapped and phase-change source lacks closure. Do not copy equations or use optimum conditions as a crack-free window.
notes: Target chemistry match does not substitute for equation correctness or internal-state validation.

claim: Longer residence at 80 C reportedly improved morphology and reduced cracking especially for thicker LFP electrodes.
material_system: LFP electrode; formulation details not yet verified
competing_explanation: Residual solvent or other property changes may explain morphology
transfer_limit: Full text formulation metrics and crack statistics are unavailable in this review round.
notes: Excluded from quantitative fitting and equation support.

claim: Spatial heat-transfer-coefficient variation can create coexisting wet and dry regions on one electrode.
competing_explanation: Initial coating-thickness nonuniformity can produce a similar pattern
transfer_limit: Apparatus differs but boundary-mapping principle transfers directly.
notes: Supports mapping set points to local Ts and J.

claim: Dryer scale-up should match film-temperature and transfer-driving histories rather than fan and temperature set points.
competing_explanation: Unmodelled chemistry-specific internal resistance can break similarity
transfer_limit: Replace water-vapor exhaust descriptors with NMP partial pressure and recovery conditions.
notes: Core basis for a two-layer device/material process window.

claim: Airflow dilution circulation and recovery make the gas-side NMP load part of the drying boundary and energy system.
competing_explanation: Local film resistance may dominate at late drying
transfer_limit: Does not directly measure crack mechanisms or local gas concentration.
notes: Justifies recording exhaust/recirculation and gas NMP concentration.

claim: Multi-zone histories can change peak solvent flux and energy even at comparable total removal; an average temperature is insufficient.
competing_explanation: Mechanical path effects are not included
transfer_limit: Use for thermal load histories only; fracture path dependence still needs experiment.
notes: Supports P0/P1/P2 schedule comparison at matched endpoint.

claim: Evaporation convection Brownian diffusion and sedimentation formed distinct particulate-coating regimes describable with Péclet and sedimentation scales in a monodisperse silica system.
source_location: local PDF pp.2–3 equations pp.8–10 validation and p.6 skin limitation
competing_explanation: Aggregation yield stress and non-Brownian transport dominate commercial slurry
transfer_limit: LFP CB and PVDF need separate effective diffusivities fixation and sedimentation terms. The source skin is a concentration-defined surface layer with no evaporation permeability or rheology feedback and is not project Skin+.
notes: Supports species-specific rather than single slurry Pe.

claim: Critical cracking pressure/stress is strongly influenced by flaws; a smooth elastic energy model can provide only a lower-bound style prediction.
competing_explanation: Plasticity heterogeneity and interface slip shift the threshold
transfer_limit: Different loading protocol from evaporation; transfer defect sensitivity not numerical stress.
notes: Motivates probabilistic defect population in CCT calibration.

claim: For an adhered channel crack the transferable energy structure is G proportional to sigma squared times H divided by plane-strain modulus; propagation requires G at least Gamma_c.
source_location: local PDF p.6 Eq.2; special constitutive results pp.9–11
support_status: supported as framework; absolute stress mismatch
competing_explanation: Plastic dissipation interface slip and gradients alter the geometry factor and resistance
transfer_limit: Only the general energy structure transfers. H^-2/3 and coefficients are source-system-specific and measured critical stress was about three times the model value.
notes: Basis of time-dependent Hc(t) rather than a fixed material constant.

claim: Drying-colloid crack-opening fields contain substantial irreversible/plastic deformation and cannot be represented by purely elastic fracture alone.
competing_explanation: Viscoelastic rather than plastic dissipation may dominate PVDF-rich networks
transfer_limit: Requires state-dependent apparent fracture energy or explicit dissipation in LFP.
notes: Warns against using final dry elastic modulus alone.

claim: Fracture toughness and critical energy release rate can vary strongly with particle size and evaporation rate in a given colloid.
competing_explanation: Pore throat modulus defect size and packing all co-vary
transfer_limit: Reported exponents are not universal and must not be fitted directly to LFP D50.
notes: Supports multichannel particle-size modeling.

claim: Cracking stress decreased with film thickness but was insensitive to particle size over the tested latex range.
competing_explanation: Size range and material toughness may hide particle effects
transfer_limit: Reinforces that D50 alone cannot set the LFP threshold.
notes: Interpret together with E020 rather than choose one universal sign.

claim: Plasticization changed peak drying stress by roughly an order of magnitude in the studied nonaqueous ceramic tape even with related particulate formulation.
competing_explanation: Differences in packing or adhesion may contribute
transfer_limit: Transfers the importance of wet-state relaxation not the PVB values.
notes: Supports measuring tau_r near locking.

claim: Particles dominated early stress rise while latex properties strongly affected residual stress; smaller alumina increased peak stress in the studied system.
competing_explanation: PVDF dissolves/precipitates rather than coalesces as latex
transfer_limit: Role separation is a testable LFP hypothesis not a direct conclusion.
notes: Motivates independent capillary-loading and relaxation/resistance submodels.

claim: Simultaneous mass saturation stress and imaging revealed a stress peak near crack onset and two-stage curvature/stress release; a ZnO system showed a finite CCT interval.
geometry_and_scale: side-walled cantilever; tens of um CCT
competing_explanation: Stress relaxation without cracking can also lower curvature
transfer_limit: Numerical stress and CCT are ZnO-specific. Cantilever inversion assumes a continuous coating; after cracking the rapid drop is an event/comparison signal not an intact-film absolute stress.
notes: Methodological benchmark for synchronized stress imaging and drying experiments.

claim: A polymer-rich surface can cross a gel threshold and become a low-permeability poroelastic skin while the underlying solution remains liquid.
competing_explanation: Particle jamming or gradual permeability gradient can mimic a skin
transfer_limit: Use only after a distinct surface permeability/modulus transition is observed in LFP.
notes: Defines an operational skin rather than inferring it from a smooth surface.

claim: Bubbles appeared after skin formation; skin thickness pressure and bubble trajectories were measured while mixed solvent-vapor/dissolved-air composition and diffusion control were inferred rather than compositionally measured.
source_location: local PDF pp.3–7; R proportional to sqrt(t-tau) in Eq.8
support_status: supported for sequence; gas composition remains inferred
competing_explanation: Pre-existing trapped air or cavitation can yield similar voids
transfer_limit: Pure polymer has no particulate pore throat; transfer as competing hypothesis only. Do not repeat the conclusion-section radius-squared wording that conflicts with Eq.8.
notes: Strong basis for separating measured bubble trajectory from inferred chemistry and mechanical internal crack.

claim: A multicomponent diffusion model including cross terms predicts gas supersaturation and is consistent with degassing reducing bubbles.
competing_explanation: Entrained macrobubbles can also respond to degassing
transfer_limit: NMP/PVDF/LFP diffusion and solubility data are unknown.
notes: Makes degassing a diagnostic intervention not proof of one bubble pathway.

claim: Internal solvent boiling/blistering is governed by local vapor/total pressure and composition rather than oven temperature versus pure-solvent boiling point alone.
competing_explanation: Dissolved gas cavitation or trapped solvent can blister below bulk boiling
transfer_limit: PVDF/NMP activity capillarity and shell resistance must be measured.
notes: Prevents the incorrect rule that sub-boiling oven temperature excludes vapor-related voids.

claim: Evaporation-induced surface-tension gradients can drive Marangoni redistribution and later corrugation while the coating remains mobile.
competing_explanation: Skin buckling bubble inflation or collapse can produce similar roughness
transfer_limit: Requires timing before mechanical lock and relevant NMP/slurry surface-tension gradients.
notes: Use timing and orientation/wavelength to distinguish from post-skin wrinkling.

claim: Cavitation and fracture can occur sequentially or in a coupled manner in a constrained drying hydrogel; cavity deformation can concentrate stress.
competing_explanation: Gas exsolution rather than negative-pressure cavitation
transfer_limit: A mature continuous gel differs from a forming particulate electrode skeleton.
notes: Supports retaining cavity and crack as coupled but distinct event labels.

claim: Bubble nucleation and stable growth are separate conditions controlled by liquid tension pore-entry pressure cavity/throat geometry and skeleton elasticity.
competing_explanation: Heterogeneous gas nuclei lower thresholds dramatically
transfer_limit: Do not use homogeneous cavitation values to rule LFP cavitation in or out.
notes: Basis for a feasibility inequality rather than a fixed universal threshold.

claim: For a mature poroelastic layer the hydraulic pressure-equilibration time has an H-squared diffusion scaling.
competing_explanation: Strong state dependence and unsaturation change effective diffusivity
transfer_limit: LFP skeleton forms during drying and requires k K and storage as state functions.
notes: Explains why thickness can amplify pressure disequilibrium faster than linearly.

claim: In the tested fine-grained soils cracks commonly appeared near the onset of desaturation under constrained shrinkage.
competing_explanation: Different soils and constraints shift the event
transfer_limit: Transfer only the need to compare cracking with air-entry/desaturation timing.
notes: Not a universal LFP air-entry criterion.

claim: Layer thickness and basal friction jointly altered desiccation-crack dimensions evolution and buried-crack initiation in clay layers.
source_location: GEO03 local PDF pp.12–16 and 20–24 plus GEO04 experiments
competing_explanation: Drying gradients and defect distributions also co-vary
transfer_limit: Aluminium adhesion/slip must replace soil basal-friction parameters. GEO03 crack-area metric can include edge detachment so internal cracks edge shrinkage and delamination must be separated.
notes: Supports joint calibration of interface constraint and coating thickness.

claim: Unsaturated transport can be coupled to moisture-dependent tensile/cohesive fracture to model crack initiation and propagation.
competing_explanation: Phase-field discrete or strength-only models can fit some patterns
transfer_limit: All hydraulic mechanical and cohesive laws must be reidentified for LFP/NMP.
notes: Potential level-2 model after level-1 parameters are identifiable.

claim: A phase-field model can qualitatively reproduce heterogeneity-influenced crack paths while local strain agreement with experiment remains imperfect.
competing_explanation: Unresolved heterogeneity or constitutive error drives mismatch
transfer_limit: Do not introduce phase field before the target question requires crack topology.
notes: Supports a data-triggered upgrade criterion.

claim: A retention curve and saturation-dependent relative permeability are required to close unsaturated liquid transport.
competing_explanation: Network/percolation or pore-scale closures may fit electrodes better
transfer_limit: Never transfer van Genuchten soil parameters to LFP/NMP; fit a suitable relation from electrode data.
notes: Use as a model-family precedent only.

claim: The sign of solids-content influence on cracking may be non-monotonic because solvent inventory/shrinkage improve while locking timing rheology degassing and pore-throat structure can worsen.
material_system: target LFP formulation not directly isolated
competing_explanation: A monotonic effect may hold over the plant's narrow formulation interval
transfer_limit: Requires two complementary experiments: fixed dry loading and fixed wet thickness.
notes: This is an explicit project inference not a reported result from one paper.

claim: Thickness raises risk through at least component Pe proportional to H hydraulic equilibration time proportional to H squared and channel-crack energy release proportional to H; defect opportunity may also grow with sampled volume.
material_system: multiple battery colloid and poroelastic systems
competing_explanation: Thickness also changes actual Ts J porosity and interface stress
transfer_limit: Scaling exponents rely on simplified regimes and state-dependent parameters.
notes: Explains narrowing process windows without asserting a universal critical loading.

claim: A final two-dimensional mid-layer void cannot uniquely distinguish entrained gas dissolved-gas/solvent bubble negative-pressure cavitation or a true internal cohesive crack.
material_system: battery polymer coating and gel systems
competing_explanation: Sectioning artifacts and normal pore clusters add further ambiguity
transfer_limit: Requires time-resolved 3D connectivity crack-tip and degassing evidence in LFP.
notes: Quality grouping is acceptable but mechanism labels must remain separate.

claim: Coating width enters local crack risk mainly through cross-web variation in wet thickness Ts J gas NMP load and mechanical constraint rather than as an intrinsic material parameter.
material_system: battery drying and general convection dryers
geometry_and_scale: batch to 120–150 mm pilot; general nozzle fields
competing_explanation: Large-area flaw statistics can create an additional width effect
transfer_limit: Needs cross-web co-location measurements on the 20 cm LFP line.
notes: Justifies parameterized 1D columns before full y-z modeling.

claim: No source in this review simultaneously provides commercial-like LFP/PVDF/NMP a roughly 20 cm wide thick coating multi-zone forced convection and in-situ internal-void/crack evolution.
competing_explanation: Proprietary industrial studies or papers outside search scope may exist
transfer_limit: A search-gap statement is not proof of global nonexistence.
notes: Therefore no literature-derived numerical process window is claimed.

claim: The coating profile and internal features can continue to move horizontally on long time scales after casting so the coating-exit state can evolve before or during shrinkage.
competing_explanation: Platform tilt or thickness nonuniformity can mimic some apparent motion
transfer_limit: Beam-direction integration small samples and strong NMC attenuation limit quantitative transfer to 20 cm LFP.
notes: Use E0 as a dynamic stage rather than a frozen initial condition.

claim: Coating shear history changes transient carbon redistribution and late drying can produce a carbon-rich top region.
evidence_nature: depth-sensitive in-situ resistivity + layered model + endpoint EDS
material_system: battery composite coating; exact target chemistry unconfirmed
source_location: dual-depth resistance histories and final elemental maps
competing_explanation: Contact-network changes can alter resistance without an identical concentration change
transfer_limit: The layered concentration profile is model-dependent and drying is far slower than a commercial NMP oven.
notes: Treat a transient depleted middle layer as a hypothesis not direct imaging.

claim: A continuum model predicts slow early stress growth faster growth after solidification and a larger surface stress than collector-interface stress in NMC/PVDF/NMP coatings.
evidence_nature: continuum model calibrated with ex-situ dry mechanics and external graphite stress data
competing_explanation: Different wet constitutive laws or capillary topology can change stress timing and location
transfer_limit: No direct wet-state stress measurement and no LFP/internal-void validation.
notes: Do not cite predicted stress ratios as measured facts.

claim: Pilot R2R cathode film temperature shows an evaporation-cooled plateau followed by a rise near drying completion and induction shifts the reported transition earlier.
evidence_nature: pilot R2R film-temperature measurement + process calculation
competing_explanation: Temperature rise can reflect several coupled boundary changes and does not uniquely mark internal liquid disconnection
transfer_limit: NMC and induction-specific coefficients cannot be copied to 20 cm LFP convection drying.
notes: Use as an E4/E6 proxy only after target calibration.

claim: Inductive energy can overheat uncoated coating defects or edges even when mean coated-film drying is acceptable.
geometry_and_scale: pilot R2R with artificial uncoated areas
competing_explanation: Pure convection may have a different local-risk mechanism
transfer_limit: Direct relevance is to induction but the result demonstrates why web-average temperature is insufficient.
notes: Motivates y-resolved edge and defect monitoring.

claim: Real-time gravimetry and film temperature quantify NMP removal for 400 and 750 micrometre wet-gap NMC/PVDF/NMP coatings and show diminishing drying-rate gains at higher set temperature.
geometry_and_scale: 7.62 by 12.70 cm doctor-blade films; 80 or 150 micrometre dry
drying_boundary: forced air plus heated bed at 60 90 and 125 C
source_location: mass and temperature results and methods
competing_explanation: External mass transfer or NMP-vapor accumulation may cause an apparent rate plateau
transfer_limit: Not LFP/R2R and no direct internal saturation stress or defect timing.
notes: Useful thermal-boundary calibration data but not an E1 mechanical-lock marker or fracture threshold.

claim: Pulse-echo ultrasonic features correlate with drying kinetics and can support feedback endpoint control associated with less final warpage cracking or delamination.
evidence_nature: operando ultrasound + closed-loop experiment + endpoint imaging
geometry_and_scale: geometry not confirmed in inspected accessible text
source_location: article highlights abstract and reported validation
support_status: supported as sensing and control demonstration
competing_explanation: Thickness density modulus saturation and porosity can generate similar acoustic changes
transfer_limit: Exact LFP/PVDF/NMP formulation wide-web scale and unique physical-state calibration remain unverified.
notes: Do not equate one acoustic inflection with a uniquely identified lock or pore-connectivity event.

claim: A validated bread model represented baking as an inward-moving evaporation transition separating a hotter drier crust region from a wetter crumb region.
evidence_nature: heat and mass model + experimental validation
target_match: low direct target match; high pedagogical value
support_status: supported in bread as a reduced-order model
competing_explanation: A finite-width distributed evaporation-condensation region can produce similar macroscopic profiles
transfer_limit: Does not prove a sharp NMP front in a micrometre-scale foil-supported electrode.
notes: Use to design front-vs-distributed-model tests not to assign parameters.

claim: Bread-core water content increased transiently during baking while crust and crumb temperatures and moisture evolved differently.
target_match: low target match; direct food evidence
competing_explanation: Sampling and local phase changes can complicate exact spatial interpretation
transfer_limit: Significant inward NMP recondensation in electrodes is unproven.
notes: Warns against assuming all internal volatile transport is monotonic and outward.

claim: Spatially resolved non-invasive NMR observed inward water redistribution in unyeasted dough under a thermal gradient.
target_match: low target match; strong method directness
competing_explanation: Temperature-dependent relaxation and water binding can affect NMR signals
transfer_limit: Chemistry geometry and vapor equilibrium differ from NMP electrodes.
notes: Supports spatial measurement rather than a single average volatile metric.

claim: Earlier imposed surface constraint changed bread expansion gas release and the depth of a dense internal region.
evidence_nature: artificial crust constraint + porosity and gas-release observation
target_match: low target match; direct mechanism intervention
material_system: bread dough with artificial surface cover
competing_explanation: The cover changes heat and mass transfer as well as mechanics
transfer_limit: Bread is positive-pressure expansion-dominated while an electrode is typically shrinkage and suction dominated.
notes: Supports asking how an early locked surface redirects later internal deformation.

claim: Bread volume and internal moisture distribution continue changing after heating and depend on the state reached at oven exit.
evidence_nature: cooling volume measurements + crust-on/crust-off storage comparison
target_match: low target match; direct food evidence
competing_explanation: Gas cooling starch transitions and ambient water sorption contribute
transfer_limit: Food-specific contraction percentages and time scales cannot transfer.
notes: Supports extending electrode observation through cooling and handling.

claim: Initial moisture gradients plus moisture-dependent viscoelastic and swelling properties generated delayed biscuit checking with full-field strain trends consistent with a diffusion-stress model.
evidence_nature: speckle interferometry + measured properties + finite element model
competing_explanation: Environmental absorption contributes to rim expansion
transfer_limit: Electrodes are foil-supported and do not normally absorb NMP from ambient.
notes: Transfers concentration-gradient to eigenstrain to stress to delayed-fracture architecture.

claim: Thicker round biscuits showed greater water heterogeneity and more checking while thinner pierced rectangular biscuits were more uniform and nearly crack-free.
evidence_nature: Karl Fischer + NIR imaging + 15-day crack counts
target_match: low target match; direct intervention-style evidence
competing_explanation: Shape piercing and formulation interactions are not fully separable
transfer_limit: Piercing is not an electrode process recommendation and food moisture thresholds do not transfer.
notes: Supports thickness and spatial distribution as separate from average content.

claim: Microwave post-baking produced more uniform biscuit moisture and reduced checking from about 61 percent to about 5 percent at similar total moisture and appearance.
target_match: low target match; high causal value
competing_explanation: Microwave also changes temperature and local material transitions
transfer_limit: Percentages and microwave treatment cannot transfer to LFP.
notes: Strong cross-domain counterexample to using average residual volatile as a sufficient quality coordinate.

claim: Early starch-cake drying was controlled by liquid transport through interparticle pores with capillary-pressure-driven shrinkage and nonlinear elasticity.
evidence_nature: pore and mechanical measurements + multiphase model
source_location: pore structure mechanical data and drying model
competing_explanation: Sedimentation and starch water uptake alter the apparent stages
transfer_limit: Starch grains absorb water deform and shrink unlike LFP and the system lacks PVDF carbon and foil.
notes: Close bridge for particle skeleton Darcy flow and capillary stress.

claim: A later vapor-transport regime associated with intragranular porosity was separated from the early liquid-flow regime in drying starch cake.
evidence_nature: drying response + pore characterization + multiphase model
material_system: starch-water slurry with inter- and intragranular pores
competing_explanation: A continuous distribution of pore scales can mimic two effective regimes
transfer_limit: Electrode aggregate-scale NMP storage must be independently demonstrated.
notes: Dual-porosity is an optional LFP branch not a default.

claim: In-situ X-ray radiography and CT observed three-dimensional columnar crack networks and evolving crack spacing behind a starch drying front.
target_match: low direct target match; strong visualization
competing_explanation: Particle morphology and boundary conditions also select spacing
transfer_limit: Columnar deep-cake geometry is outside the thin supported-electrode regime.
notes: Transfers synchronized transport-front and crack-front measurement logic.

claim: Average residual NMP should be paired with through-thickness and cross-web distributions and post-oven observations because equal averages can conceal different internal histories.
evidence_nature: project inference from battery heat/mass evidence and baking counterexamples
competing_explanation: Endpoint redistribution may be weak if NMP is already negligible
transfer_limit: Food gradients and delayed times cannot set electrode thresholds.
notes: Measure inventory distribution and history as separate coordinates.

claim: An electrode skin should be defined by a sustained surface-to-bulk contrast in permeability diffusion mechanical locking or component fixation rather than by a smooth intact surface alone.
evidence_nature: project inference from electrode counterevidence polymer skin theory and bread crust logic
competing_explanation: A continuous gradient can perform the same transport/mechanical role without a discrete skin
transfer_limit: Bread crust has chemical transformations and polymer theory lacks particulate pores.
notes: Skin+ is a model switch requiring direct target evidence.

claim: Bread dough enters baking with an established bubble-size distribution that continues to evolve through growth coalescence breakup and gas loss during proving and baking.
evidence_nature: review synthesis of primary dough studies
material_system: yeasted and non-yeasted bread dough literature
source_location: review sections on entrainment bubble-size distribution proving and baking
competing_explanation: Formulation mixing and fermentation histories strongly alter the bubble population
transfer_limit: A dough foam relies on gas cells and viscoelastic gluten whereas a normal electrode should not use bubbles as a structural phase.
notes: Transfers only the initial-condition audit: pre-existing defects may evolve after the drying boundary starts.

claim: DVC detected approximately 1–2 um above-background in-plane displacement near the future first-crack region before the crack was clearly visible in the raw CT.
evidence_nature: in-situ X-ray CT plus offline DVC
geometry_and_scale: single 300 um-gap sample on 4 mm steel pin
competing_explanation: A roughly 5 um directional full-field image-intensity artifact existed at the same early time
transfer_limit: Single sample offline DVC with minute-scale scans; 1–2 um is not a production alarm threshold.
notes: Record displacement background detection rule persistence and event-time interval before testing DIC as an early warning.

claim: Future crack and non-crack regions showed no clear difference in local active-particle count or active-particle volume at the analyzed scale.
evidence_nature: pre-crack CT particle analysis; negative result
support_status: no clear association at analyzed resolution
competing_explanation: Sub-resolution CBD defects pore throats or interface heterogeneity may control initiation
transfer_limit: Does not prove local packing is irrelevant in LFP; it rejects a simple resolved-particle-density rule in this dataset.
notes: Retain as negative evidence against choosing crack sites solely from active-particle density.

claim: Crack opening was accompanied by declining non-active-particle segmented volume near the crack and up to about 5 um displacement toward the substrate after total layer height had plateaued.
geometry_and_scale: selected 300 um-gap region on steel pin
source_location: journal PDF pp.10–11; thesis PDF pp.136–138 / printed 104–106
competing_explanation: Continued local drying shrinkage segmentation changes and motion blur also affect the apparent volume
transfer_limit: The segmented non-NMC fraction contains liquid air CBD and artifacts and is not true porosity.
notes: Couple crack opening to local displacement but do not infer pore pressure directly from segmentation.

claim: Crack-rich electrodes around 60–130 um showed better high-rate capacity than matched-thickness smooth references in the study but the crack and reference formulations differed in active material carbon binder and solids content.
evidence_nature: primary electrochemical experiment with major formulation confounding
material_system: NMC622/PVDF/NMP crack formulation 87:5:8 at 40 wt% versus reference 96:2:2 at 60 wt%
source_location: thesis PDF pp.96–98 and 112–115 / printed 64–66 and 80–83
support_status: association supported; crack-only causal claim not supported
competing_explanation: Carbon/binder fraction CBD volume wet thickness adhesion and pore structure all changed with formulation
transfer_limit: Not LFP and not a same-formulation controlled-crack comparison; electrodes were uncalendered.
notes: Report 77.7 versus 9.5 percent as a 68.2 percentage-point difference rather than a relative 68 percent improvement.

claim: The thesis image-based electrochemical model overpredicted capacity gave a spatial lithiation trend conflicting with XRD and was nearly insensitive to very large solid-diffusion and CBD-porosity changes; it could not reliably isolate crack effects.
evidence_nature: model validation and sensitivity negative evidence
support_status: model not validated for claimed causal use
competing_explanation: CBD segmentation and unresolved transport properties can make parameters non-identifiable
transfer_limit: This is a post-drying model but the identifiability lesson transfers to drying models.
notes: Require multiple time-resolved observables and falsification tests rather than endpoint-only fits.

claim: Localized operando XRD found faster lithiation near a selected long crack in middle and current-collector regions while through-thickness gradients exceeded lateral near/far-crack gradients and very high rate limited the entire electrode.
target_match: medium for mechanism; low for population effect
geometry_and_scale: selected about 195 um dry cracked electrode; two electrodes total
drying_boundary: 80 C hotplate fabrication then electrochemical cycling
competing_explanation: Gauge-volume averaging and crack-selection bias affect lateral contrasts
transfer_limit: Post-drying functional evidence only; does not identify drying crack causes or acceptable production cracks.
notes: Keep crack formation and crack-performance models separate.

claim: Cryogenic interrupted sections directly showed large pores emptying before small and surface pores and observed isolated liquid clusters and pendular rings during late drying.
geometry_and_scale: about 114 um wet and 61 um dry
competing_explanation: Cryogenic preparation and two-dimensional sampling can alter or miss connectivity
transfer_limit: Pore hierarchy and solvent differ from LFP; transfer event logic not thresholds.
notes: Direct support for separating saturation distribution from average solvent inventory.

claim: A PVDF concentration gradient was observed before strong pore emptying and before macroscopic shrinkage ended in the studied graphite/PVDF/NMP anode.

geometry_and_scale: about 114 um wet and 61 um dry

claim: In NMC532/PVDF/NMP electrodes pronounced through-thickness F/PVDF nonuniformity appeared mainly above 150 C while in-plane heterogeneity occurred at all tested drying conditions.

claim: A spherical-gel poroelastic model predicted that stronger external evaporation increased liquid-content heterogeneity and maximum hoop effective stress while a slower boundary promoted internal equilibration.
evidence_nature: macroscopic gel experiment plus finite-deformation poroelastic model
source_location: local PDF pp.8–11; governing equations pp.2–4
competing_explanation: Constitutive assumptions and spherical geometry control stress distribution
transfer_limit: Internal pressure porosity and stress were model fields rather than directly measured; free gel and large deformation differ from foil-supported LFP.
notes: Transfers the competition between external loading time and H-squared hydraulic equilibration time.

claim: As water-based graphite films became thicker their late drying increasingly departed from a gas-side linear model and an effective moving-front/internal-resistance model improved the drying-time prediction.
evidence_nature: gravimetric drying curves plus effective model comparison
geometry_and_scale: reported thickness series about 83 to 299 um
source_location: reported thickness series and drying-curve/model comparison
competing_explanation: A continuous relative-permeability decline or heterogeneous clusters can mimic an effective front
transfer_limit: The effective front was not directly observed as a planar interface; substrate and chemistry differ and cracking mechanics were not measured.
notes: Supports adding thickness-dependent internal resistance after E2 without treating the model front as literal or as a fracture criterion.

claim: High-low-high drying histories preserved adhesion relative to uniformly harsh drying while reducing drying time in the tested graphite anodes.

source_location: reported switching experiments adhesion and limited cell tests

claim: Multilayer placement gel-forming additive and wet-on-wet primer strategies improved adhesion or fast-drying electrochemical outcomes in selected water-based graphite systems.

material_system: water-based graphite multilayers Laponite formulations and primer-coated anodes

source_location: reported adhesion transport and cell comparisons

claim: Scattered-light and chromatic-confocal signals detected an operational onset of surface roughening or pore emptying during multistage drying.

transfer_limit: Thin fast coatings can yield late signals and some metrics saturate after onset; neither method directly observes internal connectivity earliest binder migration or crack initiation.

claim: Selective staining followed by EDS showed stronger top-side CMC enrichment in fast-dried water-based graphite electrodes than in slow-dried controls.

claim: Locally resolved film-temperature rise and optical appearance change coincided operationally with the detected onset of cracking during catalyst-layer drying and initial solvent composition changed drying and crack morphology.

claim: At approximately comparable calculated mean drying rates raising heat/mass transfer at fixed film temperature produced much larger crack area than raising film temperature at lower transfer coefficients.
evidence_nature: controlled process-route comparison with crack-area and count measurements
target_match: high conceptual relevance; low material match
drying_boundary: independently varied isothermal film temperature and heat/mass transfer coefficient
support_status: supported in source system; about 8.5-8.7 fold crack-area contrast reported for paired approximate rates
competing_explanation: Temperature-dependent Nafion relaxation selective evaporation solvent composition and interfacial behavior can all contribute
transfer_limit: Calculated mean rates neglect selective evaporation; binary solvents thin layers and Nafion mechanics prevent numerical transfer to LFP/PVDF-NMP.
notes: Direct cross-system counterexample to average drying rate or oven temperature as a sufficient crack coordinate; model loading and relaxation histories separately.
